case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread concerns Bluetooth SIG registration of a product acquired from another company and reintroduced under a new brand while retaining the same product design. The customer seeks guidance on registration timing, reuse of existing qualification materials, Product List model naming, and qualification administration. The consultant confirms that the existing compliance documentation can be reused, explains registration timing requirements, and clarifies how product models must be represented in the Bluetooth SIG Product List. The discussion then proceeds to quotation, fee payment preparation, and registration execution planning.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: A key topic is qualification continuity when a product business is transferred from one company to another and the same Bluetooth product is marketed under a new brand. The consultant confirms that existing compliance-folder information can be reused as part of the new registration process. The thread also addresses Product List model naming requirements, explaining that Bluetooth SIG registrations must match the actual model identifiers shown on the product label or nameplate. The consultant further clarifies that wildcard or series-style registrations are not permitted when the resulting names do not exactly correspond to marketed product identifiers.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's reasoning is driven by Bluetooth SIG traceability requirements. Product List entries must accurately reflect the model names that appear on the physical product and in the marketplace. If multiple model identifiers are displayed on the product, each relevant identifier must be represented appropriately in the registration. Registration timing is determined by the first public disclosure of the Bluetooth product, not solely by the commercial sales date.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Using model names that do not match the product label could create a non-compliant Bluetooth SIG Product List entry and require registration correction or rework. Attempting to use wildcard or series-style naming instead of actual product identifiers could result in qualification issues. Delaying registration until after public disclosure of the Bluetooth product could create a Bluetooth SIG compliance problem if the product has already been publicly announced, promoted, or otherwise disclosed.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When registering a rebranded or transferred Bluetooth product, focus on qualification traceability rather than internal product management conventions. Product List entries should match the identifiers visible on the marketed product, compliance-folder evidence should be preserved and reused when valid, and Bluetooth SIG registration should be completed before the product is publicly disclosed.
